teszt_metaadatok.tema: principles of accounting, volume 1: financial accounting ch. 5, 5.1 Describe and Prepare Closing Entries for a Business

kerdesek.kerdes: Which of these accounts is never closed?
evidence: Revenue and expense accounts are closed to Income Summary, and Income Summary and Dividends are closed to the permanent account, Retained Earnings.
Revenue, expense, and dividend accounts affect retained earnings and are closed so they can accumulate new balances in the next period, which is an application of the time period assumption.

kerdesek.kerdes: Which account would be credited when closing the account for rent expense for the year?
evidence: You have also not incurred any expenses yet for rent, electricity, cable, internet, gas or food.
This means that the current balance of these accounts is zero, because they were closed on December 31, 2018, to complete the annual accounting period.

kerdesek.kerdes: Which of these accounts would be present in the closing entries?
evidence: The fourth closing entry closes dividends to retained earnings.
Why was income summary not used in the dividends closing entry?
Dividends are not an income statement account.

kerdesek.kerdes: Which of these accounts is never closed?
evidence: It is important to understand retained earnings is not closed out, it is only updated.

kerdesek.kerdes: Which of the following accounts is considered a permanent or real account?
evidence: Permanent (real) accounts are accounts that transfer balances to the next period and include balance sheet accounts, such as assets, liabilities, and stockholders’ equity.
These accounts will not be set back to zero at the beginning of the next period; they will keep their balances.
Permanent accounts are not part of the closing process.

kerdesek.kerdes: If a journal entry includes a debit or credit to the Retained Earnings account, it is most likely which of the following?
evidence: The statement of retained earnings shows the period-ending retained earnings after the closing entries have been posted.
Retained Earnings is the only account that appears in the closing entries that does not close.
If the balance in Income Summary before closing is a credit balance, you will debit Income Summary and credit Retained Earnings in the closing entry.

kerdesek.kerdes: Which of the following accounts is considered a temporary or nominal account?
evidence: Temporary (nominal) accounts are accounts that are closed at the end of each accounting period, and include income statement, dividends, and income summary accounts.
These accounts are temporary because they keep their balances during the current accounting period and are set back to zero when the period ends.
Revenue and expense accounts are closed to Income Summary, and Income Summary and Dividends are closed to the permanent account, Retained Earnings.
